resumo: The sea, a pool, a stream or a basin in the garden. The face when a foot touches cold water is a photo you only get to take once.

itens: Check with whoever looks after her health about sunscreen and sun exposure, which changes with age.
Go early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Midday sun is uncomfortable and the water gets too warm.
Take more clothes than seems necessary: you will be changing her three times.
A large hooded towel, a wide-brimmed hat and guaranteed shade, a parasol or a tent.

secoes.titulo: The first reaction is usually not a smile
secoes.texto: A fright, crying and clinging to your neck are all common reactions. It does not mean she dislikes water; it means this is a new and enormous sensation. Go in holding her, slowly, wetting her feet first.

itens: Ask someone else to take the photos. Both your hands will be busy.
The photo that matters is the face at the instant of first contact, and it lasts two seconds.
Film fifteen seconds with sound: the noise of the water with her squeal is half the memory.
One photo of the feet in the sand or the water, from above. Simple and always lovely.

secoes.texto: Write two lines the same day: where it was, how old she was, and how she really reacted. Ten years from now you will remember that there was a first time, not what it was like.
